boundaries: Registry is not Artifact Type definition.
Registry currentness is not inferred from candidate status fields.
claim_ceiling: This candidate defines Artifact Type Registry semantics only. It does not create a live registry or alter any type lifecycle state.

scope.applicability: Maintaining one exact machine registry that maps Artifact Type identities and instance discriminators to immutable contracts and owner decisions.
exclusions: Duplicating canonical Artifact Type package bytes.

examples: Product Identity/v1 maps its schema_version discriminator to its admitted contract.
Ontology Package/v1 stays candidate and cannot appear in the admitted entries list.
domain_context.explanation: The initial candidate reconstructs 25 admitted type versions from six decisions, including seven Foundation types that use selectors in a shared schema rather than dedicated type directories.

plain_language.explanation: The registry is the single catalog that tells tools which file contracts really exist, where their exact bytes live, and which decision—if any—made each one usable.

boundary_conditions: Candidate and admitted entries are never collapsed.
Historical admitted versions remain visible when a successor becomes current.
Shared bootstrap schema selectors are valid exact bindings and need not be moved.
scientific_formal.formal_expression: entry_R(t)=(artifact@digest,schema@digest,discriminator,definitions,decision,state); registered_R(t) =/=> admitted(t); current_R(t) only by exact owner decision overlay.
scientific_formal.normative_statement: An Artifact Type Registry R is a canonical reference index over immutable Artifact Type contracts and lifecycle-decision overlays. Each entry binds one type version to its exact artifact, schema, discriminator, semantic definitions, lifecycle state, and decision evidence. R references but does not redefine or admit its entries.

notation.meaning: One exact versioned Artifact Type identity.

testable_conditions: Every registry entry has exact contract, schema, and decision bindings.
Every instance discriminator resolves to at most one admitted current type.
The registry contains references rather than duplicate canonical carriers.
